page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the ARMv8-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, supported by 64.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 1875 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Network performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several key metrics, alongside some notable limitations. The instance achieves average results in stress-ng single-core (1519.59) and multi-core (12132.09) tests, as well as in Geekbench multi-core (5360.0) and database operations (5224.61). Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 472.81 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance is a relative bottleneck, with weak scores in Geekbench single-core (937.0) and Passmark CPU (5246.06), and poor results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.19 GB/sec). LLM inference speeds are also weak, yielding 6.74 tokens/sec for a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4g.2xlarge delivers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to its 8-core CPU profile, making it a viable option for workloads requiring fast local storage access without needing top-tier compute speeds. The instance is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less appropriate for compute-heavy tasks, single-threaded processing, or large-scale machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is an ARM64 storage-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 64.0 GB of RAM and 1875 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show average multi-core and database performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 9.8 million operations per second and static web serving at 9.71 GB/sec. However, single-threaded performance and LLM inference speeds are relatively weak. Qualitatively, the instance offers strong storage-to-vCPU density, making it cost-efficient for storage-intensive workloads. It is best suited for databases, caching layers, and static web serving rather than compute-heavy or single-threaded applications.
